question: With a fresh private state and no external mount traversal, does the first uncached FUSE read of the same run-owned 85-byte Shared Drive file succeed after one hour of ready metadata/feed checks?
kind: Pre-registered clean rerun of the contaminated one-hour arm; read-only, one account and one exact file.
prior_failed_attempt: google-shared-late-uncached-live.json: accidental native-package traversal staged 26 cache files, so its supervisor correctly refused the final read. That failed endpoint remains recorded separately.
arms: A: start the installed merged binary with fresh private account state and a private Shared Drive mount; verify btrfs TMPDIR/SQLITE_TMPDIR, empty content cache and installed daemon/mount baseline
B: take at least 61 status/feed samples spanning at least 3600 seconds while doing no external traversal of the private mount and no file-content read

C: verify the private content cache is still empty, then read exactly the pre-registered run-owned file once through the private FUSE mount and require its 85 bytes and private SHA-256; require all feeds fresher than five minutes
D: stop only the recorded private daemon process and confirm its mount is gone while the installed daemon and three mounts are unchanged
endpoint: Pass only if the full duration/sample and ready/feed conditions hold, the private cache is empty before the first content read, the exact byte length and SHA-256 match, and cleanup/baseline checks pass. Record the first failure in this artifact; do not reinterpret a contaminated cache as a pass.
prediction: The previous attempt maintained ready status and fresh feeds for an hour but never reached the read gate. With no incidental traversal, the first uncached binary read should succeed; late token and collection behavior remain unproven until this run ends.
limits: One tiny file, one Workspace administrator and one Shared Drive. This does not establish large late downloads, restricted roles, 24-hour uptime or a memory trend.

observed.failure: account or feed failed liveness gate

interpretation: The clean private rerun maintained ready metadata and fresh feed samples for 57 minutes, then failed the compound account/feed liveness gate at sample 58. The first uncached file read was not attempted, so this run does not answer the registered late-read question. The supervisor did not persist which individual predicate failed. A fresh status of the installed Google connections was ready after the failure, but it cannot identify the private daemon's transient cause. Token expiry near this time is a hypothesis, not an observed cause. The private mount was removed and the installed daemon and three mounts were unchanged.
next_probe: Before another long arm, instrument the private supervisor to record only individual state/feed predicate names and numeric feed age when the gate fails, without account identifiers, tokens, URLs or provider bodies. Re-register a new endpoint and prediction; do not relabel this failed run as a pass.
